name: Regulatory, Quality and Compliance
blurb: FDA and EMA rules for AI in medicines, GxP validation, Annex 22 and the EU AI Act.
title: Regulatory, Quality and Compliance
answer: Regulators on both sides of the Atlantic now set out how AI should be used in medicine development. The FDA asks sponsors to show a model is credible for its specific context of use, the EMA has a reflection paper covering the whole medicine lifecycle, Europe has drafted the first GMP annex written for AI, and the EU AI Act adds its own duties for high risk systems.

sections.body: Treat every AI model that touches a regulated decision as something to qualify: define the question it answers, the context it is used in, how much the decision depends on it, and the evidence that it performs. The same discipline satisfies the FDA framework, the EMA reflection paper and the draft Annex 22.

developments.text: The FDA and EMA published ten joint guiding principles of good AI practice, running from human centred design to clear, essential information, for drug research, manufacturing and safety monitoring.

sources.title: FDA, Guiding Principles of Good AI Practice in Drug Development

developments.text: PIC/S and the European Commission opened consultation on a new GMP Annex 22 on artificial intelligence, alongside revised Chapter 4 and Annex 11, the first GMP rules written specifically for AI in medicine manufacturing.

sources.title: European Commission, consultation on EudraLex Volume 4 Chapter 4, Annex 11 and new Annex 22

developments.text: The FDA issued draft guidance proposing a seven step credibility assessment for AI models that produce data supporting decisions on a drug's safety, effectiveness or quality.
The EMA adopted its reflection paper on the use of AI across the medicinal product lifecycle, from discovery and trials to authorisation and safety monitoring.

sources.title: EMA, Reflection paper on the use of AI in the lifecycle of medicines

developments.text: The EU AI Act entered into force; AI in medical devices regulated under MDR and IVDR is treated as high risk, with duties phasing in over the following years.
